question.worked_solution:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ as follows: 

$$
{lim}_{x\to (3,1,2)}\,\frac{y-x+z}{\sqrt{x-z}-\sqrt{y}}=\frac{1-3+2}{\sqrt{3-2}-\sqrt{1}}=\frac{0}{0}
$$

However, we can simplify the limit by first multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (3,1,2)}\,\frac{y-x+z}{\sqrt{x-z}-\sqrt{y}} & ={lim}_{x\to (3,1,2)}\,\frac{(y-x+z)(\sqrt{x-z}+\sqrt{y})}{(\sqrt{x-z}-\sqrt{y})(\sqrt{x-z}+\sqrt{y})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (3,1,2)}\,\frac{(y-x+z)(\sqrt{x-z}+y)}{{(\sqrt{x-z})}^{2}-{(\sqrt{y})}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (3,1,2)}\,\frac{(y-x+z)(\sqrt{x-z}+y)}{x-z-y} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (3,1,2)}\,\frac{-(x-z-y)(\sqrt{x-z}+y)}{x-z-y} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (3,1,2)}-(\sqrt{x-z}+y)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (3,1,2)}-(\sqrt{x-z}+y) & =-(\sqrt{3-2}+1) \\  & =-(1+1) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $-2.$
